zones.what: Lifeboats mounted at Deck 5 obstruct downward views from Decks 6-8, with Deck 6 most affected and the obstruction lessening as you go higher; horizon views remain clear.
zones.effect: You lose the view straight down to the water but retain ocean horizon views; balconies feel less open and photo angles are limited.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to first-time cruisers who imagine unobstructed water views and photographers; experienced cruisers often accept this trade for lower deck pricing and mid-ship stability.

zones.what: Ocean-view balcony cabins in forward and aft sections cantilever past the lifeboat line, offering wider sight lines and more spacious balcony dimensions than same-category cabins elsewhere.
zones.effect: You get genuinely wider views without lifeboat obstruction and often larger balconies, while paying the same or less than higher decks.
zones.mattersTo: Strong value for anyone prioritizing balcony experience over deck height; the trade is being further from mid-ship elevators and restaurants.

zones.what: Deck 15 above holds the pool deck, Solarium, and high-traffic Windjammer buffet directly overhead in mid and aft sections.
zones.effect: Expect furniture dragging, footfall, and activity noise from early morning through late evening; worst during embarkation, sea days, and breakfast hours.
zones.mattersTo: Significant for light sleepers and anyone in the cabin during daytime; non-issue if you're rarely in your room or use white noise.

zones.what: Central Park on Deck 8 sits two decks below these mid-ship cabins, generally quiet but with occasional live music and dining activity in early evening.
zones.effect: Minimal noise impact compared to other entertainment venues; Central Park is designed as a tranquil space with only occasional acoustic performances.
zones.mattersTo: Low concern for most guests; the park's ambiance is intentionally subdued and activity ends by 10-11 PM.

zones.what: Boardwalk on Deck 6 sits directly below these mid-ship sections, with Playmakers sports bar, Johnny Rockets, carousel, and AquaTheater performances creating activity noise.
zones.effect: Evening noise from dining, shows, and deck parties can penetrate cabin floors; Boardwalk activity runs late, especially on sea days and warm evenings.
zones.mattersTo: Significant for light sleepers or early-to-bed guests; entertainment-focused cruisers often prefer being close to the action.

zones.what: AquaTheater on Deck 6 aft sits directly below or one deck below these cabins, with evening high-dive shows, rehearsals, and sound system testing.
zones.effect: Performance noise and music from shows (typically 8-10 PM) plus afternoon rehearsals; the theater's acoustics project upward through the hull.
zones.mattersTo: Bothersome for guests wanting quiet evenings in their cabin; show enthusiasts may enjoy the proximity and free audio preview.

zones.what: Main elevator banks sit in forward and aft sections on all cabin decks, with highest traffic at forward elevators near Promenade and dining rooms.
zones.effect: Cabins very close to elevator vestibules hear mechanical hums, door chimes, and hallway conversation at all hours; mid-ship cabins walk further but sleep quieter.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests prioritize elevator proximity over noise; light sleepers should avoid cabins immediately adjacent to elevator alcoves.

zones.what: I-95 crew corridor runs the length of the ship with access points in forward and aft sections, creating service cart and crew foot traffic especially early morning and evening.
zones.effect: Hallway doors open and close, service carts pass, and crew shift changes create activity noise, most noticeable 5-7 AM for breakfast prep and 9-11 PM for turndown service.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers in cabins near crew access doors will notice; mid-hallway cabins see less traffic impact.

zones.what: Deck 3 aft sits closest to propulsion machinery, where engine vibration and low-frequency hum are most perceptible when underway.
zones.effect: Subtle vibration through the floor and a low ambient hum, most noticeable when the ship is at cruising speed; lessens significantly when in port.
zones.mattersTo: Sensitive sleepers may find the vibration disruptive; many guests find the engine hum soothing white noise or don't notice after the first night.

zones.what: Bow thrusters used for docking create rumbling vibration in lower forward cabins, operating for 10-30 minutes during port arrivals and departures.
zones.effect: Brief but noticeable vibration and mechanical noise during maneuvering; occurs early morning on port days and occasionally late when departing.
zones.mattersTo: Minor inconvenience unless you're trying to sleep during early port arrivals; most guests are already awake for port days.

zones.what: Anchor chain runs through the bow, creating loud rattling and grinding when dropping or raising anchor, primarily affecting lowest forward cabins on tender port mornings.
zones.effect: Very loud metallic noise for 5-15 minutes during anchor operations, typically 6-8 AM on tender port days; unmistakable and wake-inducing.
zones.mattersTo: Guaranteed wake-up call on tender ports for Deck 3 forward occupants; higher decks hear it but less intensely.
